_comment: Hand-checked verdicts for candidates the automatic resolver got wrong. Name matching alone cannot separate a benchmark from an unrelated project that happens to share its name, so these were verified by opening the repositories on 2026-08-11. `repo` forces a match; `exclude` keeps the entry out of Benchmarks with a stated reason.

Wasp: Benchmarking web agent security ag.why: The resolver matched wasp-lang/wasp, the web framework. The benchmark is Meta's, described in its own repository as 'the WASP web agent security benchmark'.

Agent security bench (asb): Formalizing.why: The resolver matched an unrelated 2-star repository. agiresearch/ASB is the one whose description is 'Agent Security Bench (ASB)'.

Redcode: Risky code execution and genera.why: The resolver matched kyxiaxiang/redcode, which is an unrelated Claude Code project. AI-secure/RedCode is the repository whose README states the full benchmark title and publishes the RedCode-Exec and RedCode-Gen datasets.

h4rm3l: A dynamic benchmark of composabl.why: The upstream title intentionally begins with a lowercase name and was skipped by the parser's capitalization rule. The official project and repository state the full benchmark title and publish its benchmark data; the primary source defines it as LLM safety, so it is categorized under LLMs rather than inferred as an Agent benchmark from the surrounding list heading.

Vision-and-Language Navigation: Interpre.why: The embodied survey files this citation under its explicit 'Benchmarks & Datasets' section. The primary paper explicitly calls R2R a benchmark dataset, and peteanderson80/Matterport3DSimulator is the authors' repository with the R2R data and evaluation code. Publish it in both collections.

VizWiz Grand Challenge: Answering Visual.why: The embodied survey files this citation under its explicit 'Benchmarks & Datasets' section. The official VizWiz site publishes the dataset, challenge tasks, metrics and evaluation annotations, so the entry belongs in both collections.
